name: Consul
summary: A service networking platform combining catalog-based service discovery, health checks, datacenter-aware querying, and a distributed key-value store.

features.name: Catalog-backed service discovery
features.description: Consul maintains a catalog of services and nodes and exposes queries for discovering registered service instances. Registration and lookup are separate from the application protocol carried by those services.
benefits: Provides a shared naming boundary for dynamic service instances
Supports health-filtered discovery rather than static endpoint lists
Allows clients and operators to inspect service metadata
costs: Catalog freshness depends on registration and health-update paths
Service identity and tags require governance across teams
Discovery adds an infrastructure dependency to clients

features.name: Health-aware routing state
features.description: Consul health checks contribute status to service discovery queries, allowing clients or integration components to select instances according to health state and check results.
benefits: Reduces routing toward instances known to be unhealthy
Makes operational health part of the discovery contract
Supports diverse check mechanisms and service policies
costs: Checks can be stale or fail independently of application correctness
Health thresholds and deregistration policy affect availability
Additional probes and state transitions consume resources

features.name: Consistent distributed key-value store
features.description: Consul provides a key-value API for configuration and coordination data, with consistency modes and blocking queries that let clients observe changes in the catalog or KV state.
benefits: Combines configuration storage with service-oriented discovery
Supports blocking reads for change-driven clients
costs: Consistency and locality choices affect latency and freshness
KV is coordination/configuration state rather than a general relational store
Quorum availability and replication topology constrain writes

features.name: Datacenter-aware federation
features.description: Consul models datacenters and supports queries and replication across datacenter boundaries, allowing a deployment to scope local operations while reaching remote service and KV state through documented mechanisms.
benefits: Makes locality and failure domains explicit
Allows operators to choose local-first or remote lookup behavior
costs: Cross-datacenter requests add network and failure dependencies
Federation and replication introduce topology-specific operational work
A remote result may have different freshness from local state

mathematical_views.question: How do nodes, service registrations, checks, and query policies determine discoverable endpoints?
assumptions: Nodes and service instances are vertices with registration and health attributes
A discovery query selects instances according to tags, datacenter, and health state
Health observations may be delayed relative to application reality
The model does not claim that a passing check proves request success

mathematical_views.question: How do local and remote datacenter state, KV consistency modes, and blocking queries change client observations?
assumptions: Each datacenter has a replicated state domain with explicit cross-datacenter paths
A blocking query returns when a relevant index changes or a timeout expires
The model distinguishes stale, consistent, and forwarding behavior where documented
Network partitions and ACL decisions are modeled as possible failed transitions

benefits: Dynamic, inspectable naming for service instances
costs: Registration freshness and catalog availability become client dependencies

benefits: Discovery can exclude instances failing declared checks
costs: Probe freshness, thresholds, and false positives affect routing

benefits: Service-oriented discovery and coordination state share an API surface
costs: Consistency, quorum, and blocking-query behavior require explicit client choices

benefits: Locality and multi-datacenter reachability are first-class
costs: Remote state adds latency, topology complexity, and freshness uncertainty
